# Nonsimplex bipyramid cap germs and exact affine-radius descent

This is an actual nonsimplex extension of the local radial-simplex mechanism. Its active caps have conical vertex geometry but two extra body vertices lie on every critical boundary. The exact cap formula has a favorable saturation correction. The moved displayed caps need not remain minimizing normals; this distinction is retained throughout. The result is a complete finite cap-budget descent, with actual global-source control, rather than an OC theorem.

## 1. The common nonsimplex fiber and its sharp paired bound

Fix p>=2, put d=p+1, and use the centered p-simplex

    T_p=conv{(-1,...,-1), (-1,...,-1)+(p+1)e_i},
    V_p=(p+1)^p/p!,  delta=Gamma_p=(p/(p+1))^p.

In R^p x R form the bipyramid

    K_p={(x,t): |t|<=1, x in (1-|t|)T_p},
    V=|K_p|=2V_p/(p+1).

It is a convex body with centroid zero. Its p+1 equatorial simplex vertices and its two tips (0,+/-1) are all exposed: expose the equatorial vertices with the canonical simplex normals and expose the tips with +/-t. Thus it has exactly p+3=d+2 vertices and is NOT a d-simplex.

For every continuous normal (u,v)!=0 and every real h, its paired tails satisfy

    |K_p intersect {u.x+vt>=h}|
      +|K_p intersect {u.x+vt>=-h}| >=2 delta V.    (1)

Proof. If u=0, the t-marginal is symmetric and nonatomic, so the sum is V, which is strictly greater than 2 delta V. Otherwise write F_r(s)=|rT_p intersect {u.x>=s}|. Pair slices t and -t. The four tail thresholds are h-vt, -h-vt, h+vt, and -h+vt. They form two opposite-threshold pairs on the same simplex (1-t)T_p. The proved ordinary paired centroid-tail inequality, in `candidate 732b11a769399016`, gives at least 4 delta V_p(1-t)^p from their sum. Integrating t from 0 to 1 proves (1). Full, empty, and supporting simplex traces are included in that input.

Setting h=0 proves ordinary centroid depth at least delta V. The p+1 canonical caps

    u_i.x>=0,
    u_i=e_i (1<=i<=p), u_0=-sum e_i                (2)

have mass exactly delta V by slicing and cover all of R^(p+1), so delta is the actual maximum normalized ordinary depth of K_p.

They are also the COMPLETE minimizing normal menu at its centroid. A purely vertical normal costs V/2>delta V. For u!=0, pair t and -t in the own centroid cap. If u is not a minimizing ordinary simplex direction, its paired slice cost at t=0 is strictly above 2 delta V_p; continuity keeps it strictly above on an interval of positive length. The ordinary simplex equality classification therefore forces u canonical. For a canonical u, every nonzero opposite threshold displacement is strictly more expensive than 2 delta times the simplex volume: while both cuts are proper use strict convexity of (pr+s)^p+(pr-s)^p; after a full transition one whole simplex exceeds 2 delta of its volume. Thus v must be zero. This proves the menu claim for EVERY normal, including cuts through the two tips.

The same slicing argument shows that a canonical direction on K_p has STRICT paired inequality (1) for h!=0: each positive-radius simplex slice has that strict canonical paired inequality. No assertion of strictness for every noncanonical shifted pair is needed.

The active normals span only the equatorial p-space. Both tips lie in their common kernel. This is why a full-rank cone-cover rigidity statement cannot be applied to infer that K_p is a simplex.

## 2. The exact conical cap formula and favorable correction

For every r>0 and every threshold -r<=h<=pr,

    |rK_p intersect {x_1>=h}|
       =delta V(r-h/p)^d-(V/p)(-h)_+^d.            (3)

The same formula holds for every canonical u_i. Here a_+=max(a,0).

For h>=0, integrate the proper simplex vertex cap over the slice radius rho=r-|t|. Its volume is delta V_p(rho-h/p)_+^p. Therefore

    2 delta V_p integral_(h/p)^r (rho-h/p)^p d rho
       =delta V(r-h/p)^d.

For h=-q<0, 0<=q<=r, the slices with rho<=q are fully captured, while the others are proper. Thus the volume is

    2 integral_0^q V_p rho^p d rho
      +2 integral_q^r delta V_p(rho+q/p)^p d rho
    =delta V(r+q/p)^d
      +V q^d[1-delta((p+1)/p)^d].

Since d=p+1 and delta=(p/(p+1))^p, the last bracket is -1/p. This proves (3), including h=0 and both endpoint thresholds. Its correction is negative: extrapolating the isolated conical formula below the critical level would overcount the full thin slices.

## 3. Actual symmetric radial mixed bodies and all global centers

Let B be a compact convex body in R^n (with the usual singleton convention when n=0), with complete finite integer base P=B intersect Z^n centrally symmetric and containing 0. Let r^0 be positive, continuous, and concave on B, with even sampled values. Define the actual body

    C_0={(z,w): z in B, w in r^0(z)K_p}.

As for any positive homothetic convex fibers, concavity of r^0 proves convexity of C_0. It is a convex body, every sampled fiber is full d-dimensional, and

    M_0=V sum_z (r^0_z)^d,
    Q_0=delta M_0.                                 (4)

At Y=(0,0,0), pair equal fibers z and -z and use (1); the own fiber uses its ordinary delta bound. Every nonvertical ambient cap has mass at least Q_0. Purely integer-normal caps contain one whole member of each pair and the whole own fiber, hence cost at least M_0/2>Q_0. The canonical cylinders (2) attain Q_0 and cover every fiber space. Therefore Q_0 is the actual GLOBAL raw maximum.

Its COMPLETE middle critical menu consists of these p+1 canonical cylinders, with zero integer tilt. Indeed, equality first forces the own K_p cap to have its minimizing ordinary direction, already classified in Section 1. In a canonical direction, every nonzero integer threshold on any equal reflected fiber pair has strict paired surplus, also proved there. Thus the integer normal vanishes on L=span(P).

Every nonzero-base centroid is strictly shallower. The full simplex permutation group in x, together with reflection t -> -t, preserves every radial family and has orbit average zero. Convexity of depth superlevel sets therefore makes each actual fiber centroid a fiber maximum. At source z_0!=0, perturb a canonical cylinder to

    x_1+alpha.(z-z_0)>=0.

For all sufficiently small alpha, formula (3) applies in every original fiber. Its gradient at zero is

    (delta V d/p)sum_z (r^0_z)^(d-1)(z-z_0)
      =-(delta V d/p)z_0 sum_z (r^0_z)^(d-1),       (5)

because the correction has order d>=3. Taking alpha in a small positive multiple of z_0 strictly lowers the mass. Finitely many bases give a common strict gap throughout all nonzero fibers.

Y is the unique baseline global maximizing point. In its own fiber, a nonzero equatorial coordinate x has u_i.x>0 for some canonical normal; shifting that cap to the point strictly loses own volume. For a point (0,t_0) with t_0!=0, use the through-point cap x_1+v(t-t_0)>=0. Its derivative at v=0 is

    -t_0 (2 delta V_p/p) sum_z (r^0_z)^p,           (6)

which is nonzero. To justify this derivative despite the tip contacts, slice at each t. The canonical p-simplex tail is Lipschitz in its threshold with bound C_p rho^(p-1), uniformly over all threshold statuses. Multiplying by |t-t_0| gives an integrable domination. At every positive-radius slice the zero-threshold derivative is delta V_p rho^(p-1)(t-t_0). Symmetry in t removes its t term, and integral_-r^r (r-|t|)^(p-1)dt=2r^p/p gives (6). Dominated convergence is therefore explicit. One sign of small v strictly lowers the cap mass.

For any nearby positive compatible radial array, every fiber still has its depth maximum at its centroid by the same symmetry. The uniform symmetric-difference estimate

    |mu_r(H)-mu_s(H)|<=V sum_z |r_z^d-s_z^d|        (7)

holds for all halfspaces. It preserves the strict gap between the middle centroid and all other fiber centroids. Hence the middle centroid remains an ACTUAL global deepest point in a neighborhood. No exact formula for its perturbed depth is assumed below.

## 4. Exact affine-radius descent and complete ownership

Take a in L sufficiently small and put

    r_a(z)=r^0(z)+a.z.

This is an actual compatible two-sided variation on all of B: concavity is unchanged and compact positivity persists. For each canonical i use the genuine ambient cap

    u_i.x-p a.z>=0.                                (8)

It passes through the ACTUAL source Y. In fiber z its threshold is h=p a.z. For small a every threshold is in [-r_a(z),p r_a(z)], so (3) applies and its conical radius cancels exactly:

    r_a(z)-h/p=r^0_z.

All displayed caps consequently have the same exact mass

    Q(a)=Q_0-V p^(d-1)sum_z (-a.z)_+^d.            (9)

If a!=0 in L, some a.z is nonzero and its opposite base has negative value. Thus Q(a)<Q_0. Meanwhile strict convexity and even sampled radii give

    M(a)=V sum_z (r^0_z+a.z)^d >M_0.               (10)

These are exact inequalities, not an untracked order-d remainder.

The caps (8) own the whole middle fiber, because their continuous normals sum to zero there. For each other base, choose an attained critical cap at its original centroid and average its finite orbit under the full fiber symmetry group. The continuous normals sum to zero, so this genuine critical family covers its whole owned fiber. Its original mass is strictly below Q_0 by (5). Attainment uses the proved finite-base bounded-tilt lemma from `candidate 65cb1818e941a654`, Section 2; that proof applies to any bounded positive-dimensional fibers and preserves every closed cap trace.

Freeze those auxiliary families. Their incidences and own-base coverage remain exact; equation (7) and the finite strict gaps keep every auxiliary cap mass below Q(a) for sufficiently small a. Together with (8), they form a complete actual finite covering menu whose EVERY cap costs at most Q(a). Therefore the actual global raw depth D(a) obeys

    D(a)<=Q(a)<Q_0,
    D(a)/M(a)<Q_0/M_0=delta.                       (11)

The middle centroid is an actual global maximizer by the preserved source gap in Section 3. The moved displayed caps (8) are NOT asserted to attain its perturbed depth. If an all-critical owned menu is wanted, choose a fresh attained critical cap at every current fiber centroid and take its symmetry orbit; their masses are at most D(a) and the same own-base coverage proof applies. No smooth selection is required.

Scaling every continuous coordinate by [Q_0/Q(a)]^(1/d) gives an explicit body with actual global depth at most Q_0 and total mass M(a)Q_0/Q(a)>M_0. This is a strict feasible volume improvement for the original cap budget. It is not mislabeled as an exact formula D(a)=Q(a).

## 5. Fully explicit three-fiber example in continuous dimension three

Take p=2, d=3, P={-1,0,1}, r^0=1, and

    K_2={(x,y,t): |t|<=1, (x,y) in (1-|t|)T_2}.

Here V=3, delta=4/9, M_0=9, and the exact global raw depth is Q_0=4. The body has five exposed vertices and is not a tetrahedron. Let r_a(z)=1+a z and s=|a| with 0<s<=1/5. It is an actual convex body over [-1,1]. The three caps

    x-2az>=0,  y-2az>=0,  -x-y-2az>=0

have exact common mass

    Q(a)=4-12s^3,
    M(a)=9+18s^2.                                  (12)

Formula (3) is valid for all their traces because s<=1/5<1/3. At either endpoint, finite integer tilt isolates any own ordinary cap, so its maximum mixed depth equals its ordinary maximum, namely (4/3)(1+/-a)^3. Each endpoint has a genuine three-cap critical covering group; integer coefficients +/-10 suffice to isolate the displayed canonical own caps throughout this range. Their masses are at most

    (4/3)(6/5)^3=288/125 <488/125<=Q(a).

The middle centroid is an actual global maximizer throughout this explicit range, without an unspecified neighborhood. Retain the centered common copy (1-s)K_2 in both endpoint fibers. Equation (1) gives its two-fiber contribution at least (8/3)(1-s)^3 in every through-middle cap, and the own fiber contributes at least 4/3. Hence

    D(0)>= (4/3)[1+2(1-s)^3].                      (13)

This exceeds the largest endpoint depth because

    1+2(1-s)^3-(1+s)^3
      =2-9s+3s^2-3s^3 >=37/125>0

for 0<=s<=1/5 (the polynomial is decreasing there). Fiber symmetry makes the middle centroid a maximum within its own fiber, completing the all-point global comparison.

For example a=1/5 gives total mass 243/25 and an actual global raw depth at most 488/125, with a complete exact nine-cap owned cover. The new normalized maximum is therefore at most 488/1215<4/9. Its actual source lower bound is 1012/375, or normalized 1012/3645, which is greater than the OC target Gamma_3/2=27/128. Thus this is explicitly an above-target structural calibration, not a counterexample to OC.

## 6. What changed relative to the simplex theorem

The fibers themselves are nonsimplices and their critical boundaries pass through extra exposed vertices. Consequently no smooth proper-one-vertex chamber for the whole body was silently imposed. The exact negative-part term in (3) accounts for those crossings, and it improves rather than destroys the affine cap budget. Positive-rank continuous critical normals are not assumed: the p+1 active normals have rank p<d, while the tip direction is controlled by first variation and global source comparison. The complete finite ownership cover uses slack groups at the other original bases. None of these facts implies an arbitrary-fiber reduction or a below-target extremal classification.
